subject: Taxes
title: Loss Aversion and Taxes
description: Learn Loss Aversion and Taxes in one minute.

hook.text: Losing $100 feels twice as painful as gaining $100 feels good.

buildup.text: Kahneman and Tversky's prospect theory showed that humans weigh losses about 2x more than equivalent gains.

discovery.text: Loss Aversion and Taxes reveals the mechanism or argument that changes the picture.

twist.text: Withholding masks the pain. A $6,000 annual tax taken in small paycheck bites hurts less than writing one $6,000 check.

climax.text: Tax hatred isn't about the amount—it's about the psychology of loss.

punchline.text: Taxes trigger loss circuits. The pain is wired in, not rational.

quiz.question: According to prospect theory, how do losses compare to equivalent gains?
options: Losses feel about twice as painful as gains feel good
